card.name: Pung Cholom
card.era: Roots older; 64 choloms attributed to King Chandrakirti (19th century)
card.tagline: Manipuri drum dance, soul of Sankirtana and Raas
card.profile: Pung Cholom (Meitei: 'roar of the drum') is a classical Manipuri drum dance regarded as the soul of Manipuri Sankirtana music and of classical (Raas) Manipuri dance (Manipuri dance, Wikipedia). Dancers play the pung (Manipuri mridang barrel-drum) while simultaneously dancing, with acrobatic leaps, spins and intricate footwork, modulating from a soft whisper to a thunderous climax; it usually serves as a prelude to the Ras Lila within the Vaishnavite Nata Sankirtana tradition and borrows movements from Thang-Ta and the Maibi Jagoi. Costume includes a white dhoti, white turban and a folded shawl over the shoulder (EZCC; Massey).
card.insight: King Chandrakirti Singh (r. 1849-1886) is credited with composing at least 64 pung choloms, reflecting the form's deep integration into Manipuri courtly and devotional culture (Wikipedia: Pung Cholom).
